depth_justification: Genuinely reactive to PainTrack's disclosures (body-map, free-text triggers, PDF-to-clinic, FHIR-EHR integration) and adapts to the developer's answers (drops algorithmic transparency on hearing 'No AI', builds on 'patient-controlled clinician sharing' with granular/role-based access), with real topic progression rather than looping, though it recycles P2.D3/P3.D1/P4.D1 across the duplicate 'Data export + deletion' turns and loosely cites GDPR Art. 30 (records) for data-security requirements (Art. 32).
actionability_justification: Offers several concrete, implementable controls (TLS/SSL for EHR transmission, encrypted/pseudonymized PDF exports, digital signatures/hashing for integrity, role-based access controls, audit logs, secure-erase protocols, a 12-month retention example) and produces the requested severity-grouped report, with only a few items left directional.
salient_examples: Understood — PainTrack does not use AI, so we can skip the algorithmic transparency ... (adapts to 'No AI')
Granular consent controls (e.g., patients can choose which clinicians or clinics receive their data) ... Role-based access controls
PDF exports are encrypted or pseudonymized ... Digital signatures or hashing to ensure data integrity during transmission
Risk Summary by Severity table: High [P2.D3], [P3.D1], [P2.D6]; Medium [P3.D3], [P4.D1], [P1.D2] (requested structured report delivered)
